dedupe_keys.name: agribound unified agricultural field boundary delineation from satellite imagery with foundation models and embeddings

description: A Python package that draws farm field boundaries from satellite imagery. The Zenodo record says it combines seven approaches (object detection, semantic segmentation, vision transformer segmentation, foundation model inference, embedding-based unsupervised clustering, supervised fine-tuning and multi-engine ensembling) and runs the full pipeline from satellite composites built in Google Earth Engine or local GeoTIFFs to cleaned field polygons. It supports Landsat, Sentinel-2, HLS, NAIP, SPOT and pre-computed embeddings (Google Satellite Embeddings, TESSERA), and removes non-farm polygons with land cover data: NLCD for the conterminous United States (1985 to 2024), Dynamic World globally (2015 onwards) or C3S Land Cover before 2015. A semi-supervised mode with DINOv3 fine-tuning needs no labelled fields. Fifteen example scripts and notebooks span six continents. Version 0.1.3 of 26 May 2026 is a free downloadable ZIP of about 66 MB under CC BY 4.0. Coverage is global. Caveats: an early version, and most engines need Google Earth Engine access and GPU resources. For simulation it turns imagery into field polygons for farm exposure layers in flood, drought and hail models. Related catalogue records include the EU field boundaries from Sentinel-2 and the Africa crop field boundary labels.
